findings:
Pre-existing Go-against-engine divergence, measured at the base and at this head alike, in the whitespace-after-indented-code class the spec leaves to INFRA-719 and out of this issue's scope: a list item holding a typed block whose indented code ends in a whitespace-only line shorter than the code's indentation, with no empty list item beside it, is stored - Go reads the item tight (`spread=false`), the engine spread (`spread=true`). Three documents of the tester's corpus, for example `- a
  :::callout{#c1 kind="note" title="T"}
      code
     
  :::
`. The refusal the round's new lock turns on fires only beside an empty list item; without one the document is stored with the spacing a person did not write. Reported to the architect, not fixed here.

The `<!a>` class (a lower-case declaration) is still the only reading difference left in 13,780 html and indentation documents: an inline html node to the engine, text to Go. Root cause predates this change and is not block HTML - `x <!a> y` parts the same way at the fork point - so it is goldmark's CommonMark 0.30 declaration rule against micromark's 0.31. Reported in round 1, unchanged.
